headlines.title: Dell Technologies Advances Enterprise Agentic AI from the Deskside to Data Center with NVIDIA
headlines.summary: BERLIN, October 21, 2026--NVIDIA GTC – Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) announces a broad set of advancements across the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, spanning AI solutions and ecosystem innovations, new deskside agentic solutions and purpose-built AI infrastructure, helping enterprises move agentic AI from experimentation to production on infrastructure they own and control.

headlines.title: NVIDIA Introduces DSX POD AI Factories to Accelerate Europe’s Infrastructure Deployment
headlines.summary: Factory-Built With a Global Ecosystem Including Bull, Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo, Schneider Electric and Vertiv, the New Reference Design Speeds Infrastructure Deployment From Months to Weeks, Accelerating Time to First Production Tokens NVIDIA DSX POD NVIDIA introduces DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners in modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery.

headlines.title: How AI Server Demand Will Impact Dell Stock Investors
headlines.summary: Recent announcements show Dell Technologies supplying AI infrastructure and expertise to partners such as Honeywell and Accenture, while rolling out AI focused PCs, workstations and data platforms aimed at on premises and edge workloads. The scale of AI server orders, large backlog and expanding partnerships indicates that Dell Technologies is increasingly embedded in customers’ long term AI infrastructure plans.

headlines.title: Dell Technologies (DELL), What Is Driving The Latest Attention?
headlines.summary: Barclays just cut its rating on Dell Technologies (DELL), arguing the share price has outrun the pace of enterprise AI adoption, even as the business posts record results and leans harder into AI infrastructure. Recent price action shows how sharply sentiment has swung. headlines.title: What Could Derail Dell Stock?
headlines.summary: Dell Technologies (DELL) stock returned 204.4% over the year to October 19, 2026, compared with a 17.4% return for the S&P 500. Buyers at the current price are paying for Dell's sales growth to continue. During a September 1 earnings call, management said that a shortage of parts, led by memory chips, still limits the business, and it was asked on the same call how solid the growth really is. So what is that problem, and why does it raise doubts about the growth.

description: Dell Technologies Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, markets, sells, and supports various comprehensive and integrated solutions, products, and services in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and internationally. The company operates through Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) and Client Solutions Group (CSG) segments. The ISG segment provides modern and traditional storage solutions, including all-flash, purpose-built, hyper-converged infrastructure, software-defined storage, and general-purpose and AI-optimized servers. This segment also offers networking products and services comprising wide area network infrastructure, data center and edge networking switches, and cables and optics that help its business customers to transform and modernize their infrastructure and complementing its server and storage solutions; and software, peripherals, and services, including consulting and support, and deployment. The CSG segment provides notebooks, desktops, and workstations and branded peripherals that include displays, docking stations, keyboards, mice, webcam and audio devices, and third-party software and peripherals; and configuration, and extended warranties services. The company is involved in originating, collecting, and servicing customer financing arrangements and offers payment and consumption solutions and services, such utility, subscription, as-a-service, leases, and loans, as well as fixed-term leases and loans. It serves enterprises, governmental agencies and other public institutions, educational institutions, healthcare organizations, small and medium-sized businesses, and consumers. The company has a strategic alliance with Rafay Systems for the development of AI infrastructure solutions. The company was formerly known as Denali Holding Inc. and changed its name to Dell Technologies Inc. in March 2013. Dell Technologies Inc. was founded in 1984 and is headquartered in Round Rock, Texas.
